prospect.name: Rohan
prospect.occupation: Banking — associate level; in banking since 2021 with a break for a master's in finance specialising in data science; works 12-14 hour days
prospect.family_status: Married three years, currently long-distance — wife on a project in Kentucky, he is in Utah; the couple are planning to have children
prospect.training_background: Competitive powerlifter in undergraduate years with a deadlift PR around 160-180 kg; two years out after a 2021 motorbike accident; back training three to four times a week for about two years doing pull-ups, dips and squats in his apartment gym; started kettlebells three weeks ago and bought a 45 lb bell second-hand
prospect.medical: 2021 motorbike accident broke his ankle in three places; two surgeries; two or three pins and two screws remain in the ankle; two-year recovery. Walks and runs, but the ankle becomes inflamed after long walks in cold weather or extended running. Also reports lower-back pain when sleeping badly or lifting, and felt a burn in his lower back on his first kettlebell swings.

signals: Explicitly frames himself as ahead of the curve and chasing his own standard: 'compared to the rest of the world... I'm obviously ahead of the curve, but that's not good enough for me'

Treats price as a quality signal: 'I would be surprised if you would have told me that he's going to take, what, $300 a month... immediately, I would know that maybe this program is more of a cookie cutter program'
Goals are performance records (one-arm pull-up, 30-minute EMOMs) rather than weight or appearance
Counter-signal: he is not a rebuilder despite the injury history — he has already recovered and is optimising, but the deal died on liquidity, which is not typical of this avatar

goals.text: Improve mobility and flexibility as the primary objective
Regain the strength and conditioning he had as a powerlifter in his twenties
Be physically capable enough to keep up with children they are planning to have
Stay active into old age and avoid becoming bedridden
Achieve a one-arm pull-up and complete Trevor's 30-minute EMOM protocols
Get back to around 10-11% body fat
Combine strength and cardio in a 30-40 minute session at home without a gym membership
Learn correct ballistic form — swings, snatches, high pulls — which he knows he does not have

pains.text: Measurable decline in capacity — 50 push-ups became 15, 15 pull-ups became six with form breaking down
Back pulls and back pain when moving house items or sleeping badly
Ankle inflames after running or long cold-weather walks, four years after three-point fracture and two surgeries
Twelve to fourteen hour workdays plus weekend travel to see his wife leave no room for the gym
Gets bored of a routine after a few months, loses motivation and stops
Lack of a roadmap — training feels like a chore rather than progression, which he says triggers depression and processed-food binges
No qualified guidance — learned everything alone the first time and could not afford a trainer
Dual-household costs while long-distance — two homes, two cars, and $800-1,000 flights consuming the entire monthly surplus

objections.raw_quote: That is way higher than I expected.
objections.rep_response: Acknowledged and reframed on the size of the transformation — 'we're not talking about buying a carton of eggs down the street here' — then asked a clarifying question about whether it was the number or the lump sum

objections.raw_quote: even though I want to do it right now, I just know that this is not the right time for me to put down six grand.
objections.rep_response: Ran the OC isolation cleanly, offered to break the payment up, asked how much was liquid at month end, then accepted the timing frame and even reinforced it — 'It seems like if you do this, you have to literally see your wife less right now.' None of the 'not the right time' plays were run.

objections.raw_quote: So the structure of payments is not the problem for me. It's the number. It's the $6,000 figure.
objections.rep_response: Tested it once ('So even if it was a payment plan, you couldn't commit to the $6,000'), then later re-raised structure anyway by asking for his credit score and texting a PAVA financing link

offer.payment_plan_terms: Offered in principle ('in some cases we actually break it up') but never structured. Rep then offered third-party PAVA financing over 12 or possibly 24 months at roughly $300 a month plus interest.

prospect_financials.note: W2 income, no outside investments beyond payroll-deducted retirement accounts, effectively no monthly savings. Maintains two households while long-distance; flights Salt Lake City to Cincinnati run $800-1,000 each. Says he could afford $2,000 a month but the surplus currently goes on travel to see his wife. Employer reimburses roughly $800-1,000 of fitness spend per six months.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link for the programme sent — only a PAVA financing link, which the prospect declined to use
Prospect deferred rather than refused: 'in the few months, might just be getting onboarded with you guys. Because again, I'm sold on the idea. I'm sold on the program.'
Rep set a recurring touch: 'I might just ping you once a month just to see how things are going along, okay?'

Counter-evidence for a lost reading: the deferral is tied to a specific external event — his wife's project ending and the households merging — that he places four to six months out, so this is a real re-open rather than a polite no
Counter-evidence for a closed reading: he explicitly declined every structure offered and stated he would pay in full when he does buy
outcome.next_step: Rep to check in monthly by text; prospect to make contact when his wife relocates to Utah and the dual-household costs end

notable.note: The cleanest-run call in this batch on discovery and framing, and the objection it died on — 'not the right time' — is the one objection play the rep did not run a single move from. The prospect volunteered a post-surgical ankle with retained hardware and lower-back pain on his first kettlebell swings; the rep's answer was to predict the ankle would be resolved in six months rather than to ask whether anyone clinical had cleared ballistic work. The prospect also disclosed an employer fitness reimbursement of $800-1,000 per six months that was never explored as part of the structure.

quality.notes: Regular short-turn inversions, mostly at question boundaries — 'Any, any injuries at all?' at 00:17:31 sits in the Rohan block, 'Questions on the nutrition side of things' at 00:34:33 is attributed to Rohan, and 'Any questions on how it works?' at 00:38:53 is attributed to Rohan. Long blocks are reliably attributed; role read from content throughout.
